title: Unit4 consultancy and Cloud migration services - AWARD
description:
Gedling Borough Council uses Unit4 Business World (Agresso) as its core financial system. It was originally implemented in 2006 and has been upgraded three times since then, in 2010, 2015 and 2020. The system is currently used for the General Ledger, Budget setting and monitoring, accounts payable and treasury management.  Other products are currently relied upon for debtors and HR.
      
      In October 2023, Unit4 announced a strategic decision only to provide its products on a Software as a Service (SaaS) basis, and confirmed that from the end of December 2024, support for its on-premises solutions would end. 
      
      Given the criticality of the finance system to business operations, Gedling Borough Council is looking for support to oversee, drive and enable Cloud migration from our current version 7.6 to Unit 4's SaaS product.

title: BP1031 - Housing Benefit Subsidy Assurance Services
description:
Broxtowe Borough Council is conducting the procurement exercise on behalf of the Council's listed below, to establish contracts for the supply of Housing Benefit Assurance Services.

•	Broxtowe Borough Council
•	Gedling Borough Council
•	Newark and Sherwood District Council 
•	Rushcliffe Borough Council
(The Council/s)

Each of the participating Councils will award contracts separately and day-to-day transactions under the agreement will be conducted between the appointed Service Provider (Auditor) and the particular Council concerned. In any event, any formal contracts which emerge from this process will be entered into separately with the Service Provider by each council, with no relationship of joint or several liabilities between them.

The Council requires a Service Provider (Auditor) to audit their Housing Benefit (HB) Subsidy Grant claims in England, commencing with the subsidy period 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2024. (equivalent dates for any extension period), to meet the Department of Work and Pensions (DWP) requirements to give the DWP assurance of a valid and true claim. The Service Provider will conduct testing of all Housing Benefit Assurance Procedure (HBAP) aspects of the audit.

Bidders must be currently registered on the Local Public Audit Register and available to facilitate the HBAP in respect of the FYE ending March 2023 and FYE March 2024, as detailed in the LA Welfare Direct Bulletin - LAWD 12/2022, otherwise your bid will fail.

The initial contract period is 12 months. The contract is estimated to commence 1 April 2024 and expire 31 March 2025.

There will be an option to extend the contract for 24 months in 12 month increments, subject to satisfactory performance and business needs. Maximum contract period is 36 months, covering 2023, 2024 and 2025 audit requirements

Please visit the Council's e-tendering system https://www.eastmidstenders.org where you can express interest and obtain the documents, (please note we will only accept expressions of interest through the e-tendering system). Please search for BP1031.

title: BP1059 - Consultant for Greater Nottingham Centres Study
description:
Broxtowe Borough Council wishes to undertake a procurement exercise in respect of research for preparing the Greater Nottingham Strategic Plan.

Broxtowe Borough Council, Gedling Borough Council, Nottingham City Council and Rushcliffe Borough Council ("The Councils") are currently preparing the Greater Nottingham Strategic Plan, which comprises 'Part 1' of the Local Plan for each council. The Councils require a Centres Study to form a key part of the evidence base and to inform policies and strategies to be included within the Regulation 19 Version of the Strategic Plan. Each of the authorities will be preparing a Part 2 Local Plan, following the adoption of the Greater Nottingham Strategic Plan.

The study should focus on strategic and policy issues affecting the Greater Nottingham centres.

It is anticipated that the study will be based around the following key stages:

a)	Inception

b)	Quantitative assessment

c)	Review of trends

d)	Policy recommendations

e)	Draft Report

f)	Final Report

Clarifications
Bidders should submit questions via the E-Procurement messaging facility only.  Questions received by any other method will not receive a response.

The Council will seek to answer questions within five working days following the day of receipt.  Bidders are urged to submit any questions as soon as possible and, in any event, no later than no later than 10am on the 25th August 2023.  Any questions received after this time will not be answered. (Please note due to annual leave clarifications raised from the 1st August 2023 to 18th August 2023 will be responded to after the 18th August 2023).

Please visit the Council's e-tendering system https://www.eastmidstenders.org where you can express interest and obtain the documents, (please note we will only accept expressions of interest through the e-tendering system). Please search for BP1059

title: Carlton Active - RIBA Stages 3 & 4
description:
This requirement is a call-off contract using the UK Leisure Framework https://leisureframework.co.uk/ which is a specialist procurement framework supporting leisure centre building.

Pre-construction services covering RIBA Stages 3 and 4 will develop the Carlton Active project from concept design to a fully coordinated and priced construction package. RIBA Stage 3 will progress the developed design, coordinating architectural, structural, civil and MEP designs, undertaking surveys and technical assessments, and preparing the planning application and supporting documentation. RIBA Stage 4 will produce the detailed technical design, specifications and construction information, undertake supply chain engagement and cost planning, and establish the final construction price and programme, enabling the Council to reach cost certainty and enter into a construction contract.

RIBA 3

•	Refined GA plans, sections, and elevations 
•	 Updated site plans including access, parking, and landscape strategy 
•	 Coordination of structure, MEP and architecture 
•	Updated accommodation schedules and space planning 
•	 Concept visuals and external façade development 
•	 Draft outline specifications for architectural and engineering packages 
•	 Statutory compliance coordination (e.g. planning, Building Regs pathway) 
•	 Updated Risk Register and Project Execution Plan 
•	Revised Cost Plan informed by contractor and subcontractor market inputs 
•	Initial market testing of key packages 
•      Updated outline programme and procurement strategy 
•	 Surveys commissioned and summarised where applicable 
•	Design Development Pack 
•	RIBA Stage 3 Summary Report and Recommendations
RIBA 4
•	Fully coordinated architectural, structural, and MEP technical design drawings 
•	Updated and finalised accommodation schedule and internal GA layouts 
•	External works drawings and supporting documentation (e.g. drainage, landscape) 
•	Detailed performance specifications across all disciplines 
•	Fully itemised FFE and equipment list 
•	Compliance documentation (e.g. Part M, planning conditions) 
•	Building regulation strategy finalisation 
•	Final coordination of contractor-led design inputs
•	Market-tested prices 
•	Contractor proposal review and evaluation 
•	Updated Cost Plan converted to fixed-price basis
•	Final Project Execution Plan including contract readiness review 
•	Final programme for construction and handover 
•	Cost Certainty Development Proposals 
•	Development Management Agreement (DMA) sign-off ready pack

This requirement is a call-off contract using the UK Leisure Framework  https://leisureframework.co.uk/ which is a specialist procurement framework supporting leisure centre building.

The contract delivers the Carlton Active pre-construction phase (RIBA Stage 2) and will develop the concept design and establish the detailed feasibility for the redevelopment of the Richard Herrod Centre into a new Leisure, Wellbeing and Community Centre. This stage will define the project brief, confirm the facility mix, undertake technical site surveys, develop outline designs, and prepare the initial cost plan. It will also include early engagement with planning, environmental, and accessibility requirements to inform the concept and secure a clear, deliverable design and budget position for progression to RIBA Stage 3.
 
RIBA 2 
A Stage Report Pack including:
o	A detailed Project Execution Plan, outline risk register, and estimated timeline for project delivery.
o	A robust budget cost estimate.
o	Planning 'Pre-App' consultations, if applicable.
o	Review and proposal of any surveys required to develop the RIBA 4 Technical Design.
Outline Architectural Information comprising:
o	Accommodation Schedule.
o	Site Plans - Existing and Proposed.
o	General Arrangement (GA) Plans and Sections.
o	Concept Massing and Elevations.
o	3D Visuals of key external and internal spaces.
o	Outline Performance Specifications.
o	FF&E Schedule of Assumptions.
Production of Structural Information comprising:
o	Outline Structural Strategy.
o	Recommendations on the need for further surveys, assessments or investigations.
o	Recommendations on statutory and legal approvals required.
Production of MEP Services Information comprising:
o	Outline Mechanical and Electrical Strategy.
o	Outline Performance Specifications for mechanical, electrical and public health systems.
o	Preliminary plant space and services distribution layouts (including pool filtration).
o	Cost confidence MEP cost plan (based on £/m² indicative outline solutions).
o	Attendance at meetings (site-based or virtual) with coordination between consultants and key subcontractors.

title: 16+ SERVICES - YOUNG PEOPLE SUPPORTED ACCOMMODATION AND TENANCY SUPPORT IN ASHFIELD, BROXTOWE, RUSHCLIFFE AND GEDLING
description:
The Council's contract for the provision of 16+ Supported Accommodation service operating in the Locality expired on 31 July 2022. The Council has awarded new contracts for the provision of 16+ Supported Accommodation service in the Locality which commenced on the 1 August 2022, but the Council was unable to award all contracts during the original procurement exercise and a second procurement exercise commenced in February 2022 and resulted in the award of contracts for all but one of the services. However, the acquisition or development of accommodation to fulfil the requirements of the specification will take some time and as a result an interim contract was required to avoid a gap in provision for looked after children and care leavers in the south of the County (Gedling, Broxtowe and Rushcliffe) and Ashfield.\r
\r
The Council intends to create additional capacity to fill the gap in service between 1 August 2022 and the new service commencement date, through the development of an interim solution whilst the implementation phase of the new service is completed.\r
\r
The Council has identified Framework Housing Association as being able to provide these interim services and a direct award was made to Framework Housing Association.  The initial term of the contract was from the 1st August 2022 to the 31 July 2024, the contract was varied and extended in 2024 as a result of an ongoing need for provision in the South of the County.  The contract was extended until 31st March 2026.
cpvDescriptionExpanded: Health and social work services, Social work and related services, Social work services

title: Lot 1 Call-Off Contract for Care, Support and Enablement Services in Mapperley, Nottinghamshire
description:
This is a Call-Off Contract awarded further to a mini competition under Nottinghamshire County Council's Multi Provider CSE Framework Agreement (DN747717).

Call-Off Contract for Care, Support and Enablement services for a shared residential block consisting of nine newly renovated flats, located in the Mapperley area of Gedling (NG3 5QQ). Each tenancy is intended for single occupancy for people who require support to live well in their own home, strengthen recovery, and build independence.

The Service is designed to support adults aged 18 and over who have a primary support need related to a mental health condition and who have been assessed as eligible for social care support under the Care Act 2014.

The estimated contract value attributed to the Call-Off Contract/s is approximately £1,550,200 per year, however this is not guaranteed. Payments may fluctuate in line with changes to the shared and dedicated (1:1) support.

It is anticipated that the Call-Off Contract will commence in June 2026 and is awarded for an indefinite duration and has no fixed expiry date. The contract shall remain in force until terminated in accordance with the termination provisions set out in the contract.

title: Safe Accommodation Support Services for Women (Refuges)
description:
This project was a further competition procedure under the dynamic purchasing system Domestic Abuse Safe Accommodation Support Services Dynamic Provider List, project reference DN571003. It was run in accordance with the Public Contract Regulations 2015 and was a Light Touch Procurement for social and other specific services.
To ensure the appropriate types and coverage of refuge provision across the County bids were sought for three Lots.
LOT 1, South Nottinghamshire, covers Ashfield district and Broxtowe, Gedling and Rushcliffe boroughs.  The requirement was for communal accommodation, with or without additional dispersed accommodation.
LOT 2, Countywide required dispersed accommodation across the County of Nottinghamshire.
LOT 3, North Nottinghamshire, covers Mansfield, Newark and Sherwood and Bassetlaw districts.  The requirement was for communal accommodation, with or without additional dispersed accommodation.
The aim of the services is to provide comprehensive specialist support services for female survivors of domestic abuse and their children residing in domestic abuse safe accommodation.  This will include ensuring the highest degree of safety and security for survivors residing in the accommodation, offering individual support to meet the assessed needs of Survivors and aid their recovery, supporting Survivors to access other services to meet their physical and mental health needs, supporting Survivors and encouraging them to make independent decisions about their lives and being responsive to the needs of children and young people, ensuring they receive the right support to deal with the trauma they have endured.
Services will be delivered within safe accommodation, refuges, which may be individual units, dispersed housing or communal refuges.

title: Ageing Well Care Homes Framework (Round 4)
description:
Nottinghamshire County Council (the 'Authority') is seeking to add further experienced Providers of care home services (not individual care homes unless the Provider operates a single care home only) to their Framework Agreement. The Framework Agreement will be used to establish 'Call-off Contracts' with Providers who offer placements to older individuals, usually aged 65 and over, in CQC registered establishments located in Nottinghamshire (including Nottingham City).\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
A Framework Agreement is an agreement between the Authority and one or more Providers, the purpose of which is to establish the terms governing Call-off Contracts to be awarded under the Framework Agreement during a given period.\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
The Framework Agreement will be available for use by the following 'Customers':\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
âââ€š¬¢ Nottinghamshire County Council\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
âââ€š¬¢ NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire Integrated Care Partnership (formerly NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire CCG and NHS Bassetlaw CCG)\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
Call-off Contracts with Providers under this Framework Agreement may be formed by the Customers for new placements as well as existing placements in care homes in Nottinghamshire with the aim of bringing all care home arrangements under the Framework Agreement terms and conditions.\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
Call-off Contracts for 'Out of County' placements to care homes operated by Providers who are a party to the Framework Agreement may also be made under the terms of the Framework Agreement. Please note that if an Out of County placement is made to a Provider that isn't a party to the Framework Agreement that Provider must bid to join this Framework Agreement at the earliest opportunity.\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
Bidders must have experience of delivering relevant care home services and currently be providing care home services in Nottinghamshire or have appropriate services already in development. It is not the Authority's intention to encourage the building and development of additional care home accommodation through this project.
